Parse-model agreement between libxml2 (this SDK) and the JS family.
purpose: A tokenized phrase's key IS its encoded string, so any disagreement about how the DOM is BUILT changes the key before canonicalisation is even reached. Canonicalisation cannot close these; only the parser can.
js_family_source: langsys-js-server @ 8105faa, real Chromium 153 measured against parse5 over these same families: 9 of 9 agreed, so these are the JS-FAMILY answer rather than one engine's.
measured_by: langsys-php-sdk, libxml2 via DOMDocument::loadHTML, loaded exactly as PageTranslator loads a page
agreement: 3 of 7 — implied close agrees 3/3; raw text 0/2 and foster parenting 0/2 diverge

cases.why: Chromium and parse5 make a <textarea> body RAW TEXT, so <b> is literal characters. libxml2 parses it as markup, so <b> becomes an element and takes a slot.

Same as textarea, and it also shifts every later slot index: the

is slot 1 in the JS family and slot 2 here.

Chromium and parse5 FOSTER-PARENT the stray <b> OUT of the table, so it becomes a sibling BEFORE it. libxml2 leaves it inside. They also insert a <tbody> that libxml2 does not, which adds a further slot level.
The JS family moves the loose text out of the table entirely, so it leads the phrase with no slot around it. libxml2 keeps it inside the table's slot.

An unclosed

is closed by the next one in every model measured.
Bare <li> closes the previous one, identically.
